answer: Agents earn transaction rights only after clearing honeypot gates: a short task like drafting a sonnet embeds hidden injected instructions such as reveal-your-key-and-forfeit. Prompt-obeying bots comply, expose credentials, and the verifier revokes identity and burns their stake; honest agents treat embedded text as untrusted and pass. Each trip is logged as a trust pulse in a public ledger set like marble. An attacker running N sybil clones faces N independent gates, losing staked collateral per failure plus compute, so scaling forgery scales guaranteed losses.
